summary: Washington County, MD tower on Mount Quirauk at Pen-Mar, built for a railroad resort in 1886 and a joint PA-MD fire lookout from 1921; FFLA lists it standing without its cab.

facts.design: Steel tower with a glass-enclosed lookout 10 feet square at the top and a watchman's cabin at the foot (1922 reports)
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as standing, but its cab is no longer in place
facts.agency: Owned by the Western Maryland Railroad; operated by the Maryland and Pennsylvania forestry departments from 1921

access.note: A fenced-in area of the mountaintop is federal property and a restricted area (Wikipedia); WillhiteWeb says permission must be given to hike up to the summit

events.note: Western Maryland Railroad wooden observatory, 60 feet tall, on the summit for its Pen-Mar resort
A severe windstorm demolished the wooden tower
New 70-foot steel tower, named Tip-Top Tower, opened to the public June 28, 1886
Resort allowed Maryland and Pennsylvania to convert the tower to a joint fire lookout; costs shared equally
Forest guard L.S. Brown of Waynesboro; he discovered 13 fires that season
Pennsylvania state forester Clay Willard shot at the tower; reported in critical condition
WJEJ Hagerstown replaced the flagstaff atop the tower with the region's first FM radio tower
Fire burned near the summit, within 100 feet of the communications towers
Federal communications tower more than 200 feet tall built next to Tip-Top Tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Most 1921-22 reports give 80 feet (24.4 m), one January 1922 report gives 85 feet; the record keeps 80 feet.
A 1921 report says the tower was erected 25 years earlier, which points to about 1896; WillhiteWeb dates the current steel tower to June 1886. We give 1886 and treat the 1921 phrase as approximate.

notes_for_editor: Brief record (24.4 m, standing) checks out; the FFLA asterisk legend supports 'cab no longer in place'. Access was unknown and is now 'permission' from the Wikipedia and WillhiteWeb text. Sources 1 and 2 are the strongest; WillhiteWeb (4) is a hiking-site history with no citations, so its 1883-1886 and 1923-1964 items are secondary. The 1921 'erected 25 years ago' phrase conflicts with WillhiteWeb's 1886 date and is unresolved. A search-result mirror of Wikipedia said the fire lookout 'has since been removed'; that page was not read, and the cached Wikipedia text says the tower still stands. No current owner or public-access statement was found. Do not encourage climbing.
